title: Ammonia Synthesis at Low Pressure
protocol: Turn on the air dryer.
Turn on the air compressor.
Turn on the nitrogen generator.
Verify at least 800 kPa of air in the air compressor tank.
Send nitrogen to the buffer tank until oxygen level is no more than 40 ppm.
Turn on the nitrogen gas booster.
Fill the nitrogen supply tanks up to 17 MPa pressure.
Turn on the chiller.
Turn on the water deionization unit.
Turn on the electrolyzer.
Verify venting system operational for electrolyzer start-up.
Verify chiller is operational and cooling liquid is flowing through.
Turn on the hydrogen gas booster.
Fill the hydrogen supply tanks up to 17 MPa pressure.
Use computer in control room to verify emergency exits.
Check oxygen concentration in building is less than 20%.
Check hydrogen concentration in building is less than 19 ppm.
Check ammonia concentration in building is less than 35 ppm.
Verify hydrogen supply tanks are charged to 17 MPa.
Bypass the ammonia sampler and weight tank valves.
Pressurize the skid with nitrogen by setting the regulator to 2.5 MPa and opening the bypass valve until reaching 300 psi.
Close the nitrogen valve upon reaching 300 psi.
Set the hydrogen regular to 1,200 psi and open the hydrogen valve to fill the skid to 1,200 psi.
Close the hydrogen bypass valve after filling.
Open the hydrogen inlet valve and set the regulator to 10 MPa.
Use GUI controlling software to manage multiple bypass valves on the skid, compressor, and air valves.
Adjust PID controllers through the GUI controlling software to maintain a N2:H2 ratio of 1:3.
Start the skid from the control room using master GUI controlling software.
Set the reaction temperature in the reactor to 440 °C via the GUI controlling software.
Set the condensation temperature in the condenser to -25 °C through the GUI controlling software.
Weigh 3 g of the pre-reduced catalyst.
Reduce the particle size of the catalyst particles to less than 1 mm using a mortar and pestle.
Load the catalyst into 0.25 in tubing.
Place quartz wool on both sides of the catalyst in the tubing.
Increase the reactor temperature to 400 °C with appropriate ramps while flowing hydrogen through the reactor at a rate of 500 SCCM.
Continue the reduction process for 24 hours under a nitrogen blanket.
Load 80 g of CaCl2 absorbent into the absorber column (ID: 2.3 cm, Length: 30 cm).
Increase the absorber temperature to 350 °C while flowing nitrogen at a rate of 200 SCCM for 24 hours.
Increase the reactor and absorber temperatures to 400 °C and 180 °C, respectively.
Use proper temperature ramps to increase the reactor temperature.
Use transformers to make the temperature control smoother.
Keep the system in idle mode under the nitrogen blanket.
Charge the system with nitrogen to 5 MPa a few times, and then release the pressure.
Control the hydrogen and nitrogen mass flow controllers using the GUI.
Charge the apparatus to the target pressures with nitrogen and hydrogen at a ratio of 1:3.
Close the inlet valves once the target pressure is achieved.
Open the reactor outlet valve after charging.
Turn on the recirculating pump.
Continue the test for 5 hours until the absorber starts to breakthrough.
Open the inlet and outlet valves to begin desorption.
Reduce the system's pressure to atmospheric pressure.
Increase the temperature of the absorber while flowing nitrogen at a flow rate of 100 SCCM for 5 hours to desorb ammonia.
